docs.title: Welcome to sample_docs
docs.text:
sample_docs is a general-purpose MkDocs starter template for internal or public team documentation.

It is designed to help teams publish clear, structured docs without spending much time on setup.

docs.title: What this template includes
docs.text:
• A clean home page
  • A simple getting-started section
  • A reusable integrations section
  • Export guides
  • A FAQ page
  • GitHub Pages deployment with GitHub Actions

docs.title: Suggested use cases
docs.text:
You can adapt this template for:

  • Product documentation
  • Internal team handbooks
  • Operations runbooks
  • Integration guides
  • Customer help centers

docs.title: Documentation principles
docs.text:
This starter follows a few simple rules:

  1. Keep each page focused on one topic.
  2. Use short sections with clear headings.
  3. Link related pages together.
  4. Reuse the same structure across similar docs.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text: If you are setting up docs for the first time, begin with Getting Started.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
How do I use this template?

Start by editing the project name, homepage, navigation, and sample pages.

Can I remove sections I do not need?

Yes. Delete the markdown files you do not want and update mkdocs.yml to match.

docs.title: Writing
docs.text:
What structure should a page follow?

A good default is: purpose, prerequisites, steps, troubleshooting, and related pages.

How do I keep docs consistent across the team?

Reuse the same headings and page patterns for similar content.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Can this be deployed automatically?

Yes. The included GitHub Actions workflow can publish the site to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This page explains how to use the template as a starting point for your own documentation site.

docs.title: Recommended first steps
docs.text:
1. Rename the project in mkdocs.yml.
  2. Replace the homepage content in docs/index.md.
  3. Update the navigation to match your real sections.
  4. Remove sample pages you do not need.
  5. Add your own guides, references, and FAQ entries.

docs.title: Suggested folder ownership
docs.text:
A simple setup that works well for most teams:

  • docs/ for all markdown content
  • docs/assets/ for logos and icons
  • docs/stylesheets/ for custom styling
  • .github/workflows/ for deployment automation

docs.title: Writing pattern
docs.text:
Use this structure for most pages:

  • Purpose
  • When to use
  • Steps
  • Examples
  • Troubleshooting
  • Related pages

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Once the basic structure is in place, continue with the Integrations overview.

docs.title: Integrations Overview
docs.text: This section shows a reusable pattern for documenting integrations with external tools, platforms, or services.

docs.title: What to document for each integration
docs.text:
For consistency, each integration can have three pages:

  • Overview: what the integration does
  • Sync: how data or configuration is exchanged
  • Generate: what output or workflow is produced

docs.title: Why this structure helps
docs.text: It keeps similar tools documented in the same way, which makes it easier for contributors to add content and for readers to find what they need.
